title: A Landslide in Alaska Made a Giant Tsunami
summary:
In August 2025, part of a mountain in Alaska fell into the sea. The falling rock made the second-highest tsunami ever recorded.

It happened in Tracy Arm, a long, narrow inlet of the sea called a fjord. Water and rocks rushed 1,580 feet up the other side. That is taller than the top floor of Taipei 101, a very tall skyscraper. Luckily, it was early in the morning, and no ships were nearby.

Scientists at the Alaska Earthquake Center studied what happened. They found warning signs. The glacier below had shrunk a lot. Heavy rain had soaked into cracks in the mountain. Instruments also picked up thousands of tiny shakes, called tremors, in the days before.

The scientists think these clues could have warned people at least a day early. They want an alert system with yellow, orange and red levels. The U.S. does not have one like this yet.
why_it_matters: Warning systems could help keep people on boats and near the coast safe, just like fire drills help keep you safe at school.
